name: Short Spikedrop
description: Raise the spiked head above the shoulder and drop it straight down so the studs land on the crown or collarbone.

name: Holding Shaftcollar
description: Hold the shaft with both hands apart and lift it across the chest so the wood takes an incoming blow.

name: Low Studcrush
description: Swing the ball in a low arc at shin height so the studs rake across the opponent's lead leg.

name: Ballpace
description: Let the weight of the head pull the body through one short step, so the stance sinks low behind the swing.

name: Angled Shaftcollar
description: A quick upward slant of the shaft makes an incoming blade slide off the wood and pass the shoulder.

name: Straight Topspike
description: Punch the topmost spike of the head straight forward at the throat or face with a short two-handed shove.

name: Raised Spikeball
description: Hoist the studded ball from the ground to shoulder height and hold it there, shaft slanted across the body as a guard.

name: Crunchblow
description: From the hoisted stance, swing the ball forward and down to knock hard on the top of the opponent's head.

name: Burrdrop
description: When a foe closes inside the arc of the ball, jab the capped end of the shaft into his ribs.

name: Catching Thornbite
description: Whip the ball sideways so the studs scrape down the forearm and spoil the opponent's grip on his weapon.

name: Sideways Crunch
description: Slide the rear foot after each swing so the body follows the ball's momentum instead of being dragged by it.

name: Resting Headspike
description: Rest the thorned haft along the shoulder, then roll it forward to knock a thrust aside before swinging.

name: Upward Maul
description: Let the ball hang from a low grip, then swing it forward and upward like a pendulum into the groin line.

name: Pummelhit
description: Planting the front foot and driving the hips, the user lands the head with the weight of the whole body behind it.

name: Ballblow
description: Curve the ball around a raised guard so the thorns bite the ribs on the unprotected side.

name: Solid Shaftcollar
description: Sweep the shaft across the front as a flat bar so a descending cut lands on the wood and stops.

name: Crunchstrike
description: Spin the shaft once in the hand and bring the capped butt round to rap the opponent's knuckles.

name: Nimble Spikedrop
description: Let the head bounce clear after a blow, retreat one step and bring the haft back into guard.

name: Maulblow
description: Roll the wrists so the ball whirls in a small circle beside the body, then release it into the target.

name: Thistlehit
description: A sharp snap of both wrists at the end of the swing makes the ball crack down like a whip tip.

name: Kept Spikering
description: Pull the ball back against its own swing so the haft rises to turn a blow away from the body.

name: Hitching Spikebase
description: Hook a spike through the opponent's outstretched sleeve and yank, pulling the arm off its line.

name: Maulpace
description: Slide the hands along the shaft while stepping half a pace, shortening the reach to meet a close attacker.

name: Brisk Prickball
description: Strike once with the ball, then drive the capped butt at the same target from the opposite side.

name: Planted Spikebase
description: Root both feet wide and hold the shaft before the chest, letting the hardened frame carry a blow's weight.

name: Burrbump
description: Swing the head in a wide overhead arc so the spikes come down like a smith's hammer on the target.

name: Burrstrike
description: Aim a slanting downward stroke at the meeting of neck and shoulder, where the burrs bite deepest.

name: Locking Topspike
description: Cross the shaft over an enemy's sword hilt and press down, pinning the blade for a heartbeat.

name: Square Thornbite
description: After a missed forward swing, let the ball loop behind the shoulder and bring it back across at the target.

name: Blunt Studball
description: Lower the shoulder behind the horizontal shaft and charge, shoving the opponent back off his feet.

name: Mauldrop
description: Chop the head down onto the front knee of a foe who stands too far forward.

name: Ready Spikering
description: Snap the ball back to the shoulder after every stroke, so the shaft is ready to turn the next blow aside.

name: Open Thornball
description: Draw a little qi on the inhale and let it out as the orb comes down, so the swing lands cleanly.

name: Level Prickball
description: Keep the orb circling beside the body with steady breath, then rake it across the opponent's guard arm.

name: Settled Headspike
description: Turn the shaft to catch a cut on the wood, then let the orb's weight swing back toward the foe.

name: Single Topspike
description: Drive the single top spike forward into a gap in the opponent's armor with a flat, short push.

name: Lowered Ballsocket
description: Let the orb hang low in front of the knees with the shaft upright, covering the lower body.

name: Stepping Pummel
description: Time a long stride to the outbreath so the body arrives with the swing instead of behind it.

name: Balldash
description: Flip the shaft and rap the capped butt against the knuckles of the hand gripping a weapon.

name: Hard Thornbite
description: Bring the burr-studded head down in one straight line onto the shoulder or helm of the target.

name: Pummelstrike
description: Whip the head flat from the side at ear height, letting the burrs graze before the full weight lands.

name: Tight Shaftcollar
description: Cross the shaft above the head to catch an overhead cut between the hands.

name: Burrwedge
description: Snag the burrs in a shield rim or cloak and drag back, unsettling the opponent's footing.

name: Swaying Maul
description: Pivot on the lead foot so the shaft stays between the body and the foe through the turn.

name: Descending Prickball
description: Lob the thistle-spiked head in a high arc so it falls steeply onto a raised guard.

name: Thistledash
description: Hold the swing loosely and let the ball's own weight lead the arms through the arc.

name: Snug Ballsocket
description: Plant the shaft vertically at the side and let a low cut break against the wood.

name: Sudden Spikering
description: Flick the head back across the body with a turned wrist to strike a foe at the flank.

name: Thistletrot
description: Step in while sliding the rear hand up the shaft, shortening the lever to fight at close range.

name: Fixing Spikebase
description: Set a spike over the rim of a buckler and tug, pinning the shield to the foe's own arm.

name: Crunchdrop
description: Crash the bristling head down from above, using the whole length of the shaft to add reach.

name: Folded Spikebase
description: Roll the head in a steady circle before the chest so the spikes and shaft make a moving guard.

name: Narrow Topspike
description: Thrust a single protruding spike through the gap between breastplate and gorget in one short drive.

name: Thistlebump
description: Curl the ball out and around a guard, then pull it inward to land on the exposed temple.

name: Pummeldash
description: Tap the head lightly against the opponent's weapon to test his grip before committing the heavy swing.

name: Snug Shaftcollar
description: Turn the shaft a quarter in the hands so a blade skates along the wood and off to one side.

name: Skipping Crunch
description: Step off the line of attack and drop the head onto the foe as he passes.

name: Hooding Ballsocket
description: Gather the head back to the hip, shaft slanted, and steady the breath before the next exchange.

name: Firm Spikedrop
description: Turn the shaft a half-circle in the hands so the spikes land flat-faced on the chosen mark.

name: Mauldash
description: Turn the shaft backward so the ball approaches from behind the shoulder and lands on the same mark.

name: Thistleblow
description: Pick one stud as the leading point and drive it into a chalked target again and again.

name: Raised Prickball
description: Pass the shaft between the hands while turning a blow, so the guard changes sides without a gap.

name: Shifting Thornbite
description: Turn on the ball of the foot as the spikes land, so the body is already facing the next foe.

name: Turning Studball
description: Drop the shaft over an opponent's trailing leg and hold it down so he cannot step out.

name: Kept Headspike
description: Draw the ball back to the shoulder at once after a landing, shaft angled to cover the head.
